newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Clinton, China's Jiang agree to summit exchange.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, China's Jiang agree to summit exchange.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton and Chinese President Jiang Zemin have accepted each other's invitations for summits in Washington and Beijing, White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry said on Sunday.

"The two presidents have accepted each other's invitations for state visits," McCurry said after an 85-minute Clinton-Jiang meeting on the fringes of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) conference in the Philippines.
He said the time and the sequence of the state visits are still to be determined.
McCurry called the meeting constructive and said it had "moved the vital (Sino-American) strategic relationship forward."

The United States and China have had very stormy relations since Beijing cracked down on pro-democracy activists in Tiananmen Square in 1989. The two countries in recent months have made a concerted effort to resume more constructive ties that will ensure cooperation into the next century.
